newsitem.title: UK: Designer wear Ted Baker seeks float on LSE in July.
newsitem.headline: Designer wear Ted Baker seeks float on LSE in July.

text.p: Clothing designer and retailer Ted Baker Plc said on Thursday it planned a flotation on the London Stock Exchange in July and would look to improve its presence in Europe and the United States.
Ted Baker said it hoped to raise around 25 million stg from a placing by Charterhouse Tilney Securities Ltd which would value the company at between 50 and 62 million stg.
The company designs, wholesales and retails shirts, knitwear, jeans and jackets which are sold in the UK through its seven stores, a concession in Harrods and selected retailers.
Its products include Ted Baker shirts for men, Teddy Baker Woman casual wear for women and the Teddy Boy range aimed at the three to 14 year old boyswear market.
The company also sells to specific retailers in the U.S. and has two Ted Baker stores in Amsterdam and Zurich.
Ted Baker said it intended to expand in Europe through retail and wholesale franchise agreements and would raise its profile in the U.S. by developing its wholesale network.
The company increased its operating profits in the year to January 25 1997 to approximately 4.2 million stg from 1.4 million for the same period in 1996.
The 1997 operating profit figure excluded a one-off payment of 2.9 million stg to the chief executive and founder Ray Kelvin.
